data.name: Mussaverso O Jogo
data.detailed_description:
Uma homenagem moderna aos clássicos dos anos 90 — com muita ação, plataformas e a bagunça do Mussaverso!

W, o Mussa Reverso, e seus Wlóides invadiram o universo do Mussa e viraram tudo de cabeça para baixo! Agora, Mussa precisa embarcar em uma aventura por diferentes mundos para enfrentar os invasores e acabar com essa confusão.

Mussaverso O Jogo é uma aventura de ação e plataforma 2.5D que combina cenários tridimensionais, desafios inspirados nos clássicos dos anos 90 e o humor do universo do Mussa. Prepare os microfones, calcule seus saltos e entre nessa aventura!

Muito além dos pulos

Cada trecho da jornada traz uma maneira diferente de encarar os desafios. Arremesse microfones contra os inimigos, monte no camelo, deslize pelos trilhos, nade entre piranhas e enfrente tempestades de areia. Entre plataformas, obstáculos e mudanças de ritmo, o Mussa vai precisar de mais do que um bom salto para seguir em frente!

W chegou. E trouxe companhia.

O Mussa Reverso não veio sozinho: seus Wlóides estão espalhando o caos pelo Mussaverso. Além dos invasores, criaturas e armadilhas dos próprios cenários tornam o caminho ainda mais perigoso. Observe os inimigos, escolha a hora de atacar e tome cuidado com o próximo passo!

Chefes à moda antiga

Grandes adversários, ataques para aprender e oportunidades para contra-atacar. As batalhas contra chefes colocam suas habilidades à prova e resgatam aquele prazer de entender o desafio depois de algumas tentativas — e finalmente vencer!

Domine cada fase

Preste atenção nos detalhes, descubra caminhos mais vantajosos e aprenda a superar os obstáculos. Colete moedas, abasteça seu estoque de microfones e aproveite os recursos pelo caminho para avançar. Conhecer bem uma fase pode fazer toda a diferença entre ficar pelo caminho e chegar ao final!

Uma nova aventura no universo do Mussa

Anteriormente conhecido como Mussoumano: Ataque dos Haters, o projeto entra em uma nova fase como Mussaverso O Jogo, com uma aventura reformulada e W no centro de toda a confusão.

Acesso Antecipado

A versão atual inclui a primeira fase reformulada. Planejamos adicionar as demais fases e suas mecânicas gradualmente nas atualizações. Compartilhe suas impressões na Comunidade Steam e participe dessa nova etapa!

reviews.review:
At its best, it offers glimpses of classic platforming nostalgia, but at its worst, it stumbles headfirst into design decisions that could make even the most patient players rage quit.

The premise is simple: You play as a successful streamer who receives a golden plaque in recognition of his achievements. But the celebration is cut short when the prized plaque is stolen, prompting our hero to chase down the evildoers responsible. While this setup may appeal to those familiar with the character’s online presence, newcomers are left without any meaningful introduction, reducing him to a generic platforming protagonist.

Controls are basic but serviceable. You can move left or right, jump, and attack using two moves: a stomp and a microphone throw. The stomp is only usable mid-jump, while the microphone toss requires collecting microphones scattered throughout the stage. 

The collectibles include hearts (granting extra hits), coins (used for purchases), and microphones. Your microphone stash carries over to other stages, but only if you complete the stage. The same goes for coins, which can be spent at shops between stages to purchase extra lives and microphones. However, the game never keeps track of how many coins there are in a stage, so there’s no need to find them all.

Where the game falters is in its platforming mechanics. The jump feels both floaty and slippery, often resulting in overshooting platforms or sliding off edges at the worst possible moment. The sensation of constantly bouncing off ledges because you missed by an inch is aggravating and becomes a frequent death sentence when pits result in instant death.

This slippery precision feels counterproductive, especially when compared to the enemy damage system. Taking damage from foes only removes a heart, but falling into pits is unforgiving. With the game aiming for tough, precise platforming, this discrepancy makes deaths feel cheap rather than challenging. The lives system further compounds the frustration. Run out of lives, and the game offers you five continues before it's back to the title screen. 

Stages are accessed from a top-down view where you guide the character to stage nodes. It’s a neat touch, but ultimately pointless. There’s little to do beyond breaking a lucky pot for extra lives or visiting the shop. Worse yet, after defeating a stage boss, previous areas become locked, preventing players from returning to earlier stages.

The stages are well-designed visually, fitting the game's overall setting and theme. Occasionally, you’ll find hidden paths or secrets, which offer some satisfaction in discovery. The enemies, while not particularly varied, do a competent job of providing minor obstacles. They are separated into animals and human enemies. 

Perhaps the most baffling design choice is the achievement system. Its progress-tracking is tied to the same frustrating checkpoint system. Achievements only register progress when you successfully complete a stage. Die along the way, and all progress is erased.

To make matters worse, many of these achievements revolve around basic actions like jumping, throwing microphones, or collecting coins. Yet, by stage 8, I had only jumped 80 times, thrown a microphone three times, and gathered a mere 35 coins. With death so frequent and unforgiving, any attempt at earning achievements is completely pointless.
